what-virtualization-is-and-hypervisor-ty.r: A team could not start any guest on a new server. The image was blamed for an hour. The real cause was a firmware setting: hardware virtualization was off, so the kvm module could not load. After they enabled it, every guest started.
what-virtualization-is-and-hypervisor-ty.x: Treat the hypervisor as a stack: CPU features, kvm, QEMU, libvirt. Faults at the bottom hide behind errors at the top, so check lsmod and /proc/cpuinfo before touching guest images, and use virtio drivers by default.

cpu-memory-and-overcommit.r: Web guests slowed every Monday at 09:00 while their own graphs showed low CPU. Steal time was 41 percent: a weekly report batch shared the same host. Moving the batch guests and setting a 3 to 1 vCPU limit fixed it.
cpu-memory-and-overcommit.x: Guest metrics lie about contention. Alert on steal or ready time and on host swap, set overcommit ratios per cluster by workload class, and keep latency-sensitive guests on hosts with headroom and NUMA-aligned sizes.

virtual-disks-snapshots-and-templates.r: A storage pool went from 60 percent to full in two days. A backup tool made an hourly snapshot of a database guest and never deleted them. Merging the old snapshots freed 180 GiB, and a retention rule plus an 80 percent alert were added.
virtual-disks-snapshots-and-templates.x: Snapshot chains trade space and read speed for a rollback point. Enforce retention in the tool that creates them, monitor pool allocation against capacity including thin overcommit, and test restores from real backups, not snapshots.

virtual-networking-bridges-and-vlans.r: A new guest got no DHCP address and the DHCP server was blamed. The guest was on VLAN 40 but the uplink trunk carried only VLANs 20 and 30. Adding VLAN 40 to the trunk fixed it.
virtual-networking-bridges-and-vlans.x: Debug virtual networks hop by hop: guest NIC, vnet port, bridge, uplink, switch. Check VLAN membership on each, keep MACs unique across clones, and document which networks are bridged, routed or NAT.

live-migration-ha-and-troubleshooting.r: Draining one host for patching failed to migrate a guest because the target was almost out of memory, and HA then restarted two guests on it, exhausting memory. The team capped host memory use at 80 percent and drained one host at a time.
live-migration-ha-and-troubleshooting.x: Design clusters for the failure case: N+1 capacity counted in memory, a common CPU model, reliable fencing and quorum. Check the six basics (virtualization, memory, storage, disk files, network, steal) before blaming a guest.

virtualization-ops-capacity-overcommit-a.r: Every Monday at 09:00 unrelated servers on one host slowed for twenty minutes. A weekly batch guest with 16 vCPUs took the cores on a 40-core host. Moving it to a dedicated pool with CPU shares ended the stalls.
virtualization-ops-capacity-overcommit-a.x: Judge by measured contention, not by the ratio. Keep N+1 headroom to evacuate the largest host and move guests early when pressure trends upward.

virtualization-ops-libvirt-and-kvm-day-t.r: A database guest got slower every week and finally froze when its datastore filled. Each change had left another snapshot, and the chain was nine layers deep. Merging the chain and limiting snapshots to 72 hours with an owner fixed the pattern.
virtualization-ops-libvirt-and-kvm-day-t.x: Snapshots are not backups and long chains hurt. Live migration depends on compatible CPUs, storage and bandwidth, so keep a pool of similar hosts and check capacity before every drain.

virtualization-ops-guest-performance-tro.r: File transfers between two guests on the same host reached only a fraction of the network speed. The guest used the emulated e1000 card with a single queue. Switching to virtio with multiqueue raised throughput several times and ended the drops.
virtualization-ops-guest-performance-tro.x: Many guests slowing together point below them. One slow guest points to its own configuration, and emulated devices are a common silent cause of poor throughput.

vm-backup-replication-and-recovery.r: A hypervisor snapshot was kept as the only backup and grew until it filled the datastore. A scheduled backup to separate storage with tested restores replaced it.
vm-backup-replication-and-recovery.x: A snapshot is a short-lived rollback point, not a backup. Backups need separate storage, consistency and regular restore tests.

vm-templates-cloud-init-and-image-pipeli.r: A golden template built two years earlier still contained an old SSH key and missing patches. Rebuilding it monthly in a pipeline kept images current and reviewable.
vm-templates-cloud-init-and-image-pipeli.x: Images are artifacts with a supply chain. Build them from code, scan and sign them, and retire old versions on a schedule.

gpu-passthrough-and-device-assignment.r: A passthrough GPU froze the host on VM shutdown because it did not reset cleanly. Choosing a supported reset method and testing shutdown and restart cycles solved it.
gpu-passthrough-and-device-assignment.x: Passthrough trades flexibility for performance. Know that the device is dedicated, test reset and failure paths and weigh it against sharing options such as vGPU or MIG.

hypervisor-security-and-isolation.r: The management interface of a hypervisor was reachable from the guest network. A compromised guest could probe it. Moving management to an isolated network behind a jump host removed the exposure.
hypervisor-security-and-isolation.x: Virtualization isolation is strong but not absolute. Defense in depth means separating by trust level and keeping the control plane far from guests.
